title: skill-feedback-issue: reports cannot say whether the fix or only the symptom was verified (GH#8)
description: The body template puts 'Where it comes from' (a line number, cheap to confirm by reading) directly next to 'Proposed fix' (not confirmable by reading at all), with no field distinguishing what was actually established. Step 1 says 'confirm each claim at a line number', which covers the symptom only. A reader takes 're-verified against the installed source' as covering the whole report. Reported consequence: three of five issues filed by this skill against godot-selftest-harness carried a proposed fix that would not have fixed the bug, each caught only because the implementer reproduced the mechanism before applying the diff.
acceptance_criteria: A Verified field with an honest default, a step 1 sentence separating symptom-confirmation from fix-correctness, and an evidence-bar clause that a checkable fix gets checked. Composes with the Environment line's spotted-by rather than duplicating it.
close_reason: Shipped for GH#8 as the Verified field plus the step 1, evidence-bar, guardrail and report-back clauses.

title: skill-feedback-issue: installPath is not necessarily the directory the skill ran from (GH#7 item 1)
description: Step 1 resolves installPath from installed_plugins.json and says to re-verify there. The cache keeps every version ever installed side by side - eight for this plugin right now - and the directory a skill loads from is not guaranteed to be the one installed_plugins.json records. This is the one skill whose entire premise is that a stale install produces false alarms, so a line number confirmed in a tree that did not execute is that exact failure arriving through the front door. Verified: 0.6.0 vs 0.10.0 differ by a whole skill plus eight templates.
acceptance_criteria: The reconciliation is mechanical, not a paragraph the reader may skip, and it answers whether the skill's own files differ between the two versions.
close_reason: Shipped for GH#7 as resolve_skill.py plus the step 1 rewrite; 8/8 behaviour cases pass including the reported 0.6.0-vs-0.10.0 scenario.

title: godot-game-ui: six art-direction colours in ui_theme.gd bodies are unreachable by a re-skin
description: style_button base/hover/press/primary-ink, slot_box active/inactive and badge_box inactive are Color literals inside function bodies. --palette only substitutes the 16 PALETTE consts, and the file's own header says re-skinning means 'change the PALETTE and TYPE blocks. Nothing else.' Two of them exactly duplicate a palette constant (slot_box inactive == PANEL_FILL, button press == SLOT_EMPTY). Under --palette clinical (light panels, near-black TEXT) the secondary buttons render near-black ink on a dark grey fill.
acceptance_criteria: Every one derives from a palette constant; amber output stays visually equivalent; palette_lint clean.
close_reason: Shipped for GH#5; verified by both smoke tests, juice_test, palette_lint on both kits, and a WCAG contrast probe across all six palettes.

title: godot-game-ui: ship palette_lint.py (GH#5 item 1)
description: Nothing detects a hard-coded Color literal that duplicates a palette constant: against the shipped palette the literal and the constant are numerically identical, so no runtime assertion can tell them apart. The distinction only exists in the source, so the check has to be a source lint. Stdlib-only, runs over the kit's templates AND over a scaffolded project's ui dir.
acceptance_criteria: Exits 1 naming file:line for a chromatic Color literal outside ui_theme.gd, and for any literal in ui_theme.gd whose RGB duplicates a palette constant. Shown to FAIL against the leaks that exist today.
close_reason: Shipped for GH#5; verified by both smoke tests, juice_test, palette_lint on both kits, and a WCAG contrast probe across all six palettes.

title: itch-ci-deploy: skill + scaffolder for Godot->itch.io CI deploy
description: New skill extracted from Gather's deploy-to-itchio.yml. Template + scaffold_itch_deploy.py (measures version/preset/thread_support/gitignore/renderer, --check audit). Bumps plugin to 0.14.0.

title: Lint SKILL.md Markdown (log S-043)
description: SKILL.md is the product in this repo, so a rendering bug is a defect in the deliverable. A **bold** paragraph placed immediately after a list item with no blank line is absorbed into that bullet as a lazy continuation - introduced one this session and caught it only by reading the diff. Nothing lints Markdown here.
acceptance_criteria: Stdlib-only script in the palette_lint.py mould covering lazy continuations, unclosed fences and headings without a preceding blank line. Shown to FAIL on the bug that prompted it, and shown silent on all current SKILL.mds.

title: skill-feedback-issue: re-verify step is sold as a defence, not as where you find the repo's own argument (GH#7 item 2)
description: Reading the target's source to confirm line numbers reliably turns up the place the repo already states the principle your fix depends on, applied somewhere else. A report quoting the maintainer's own convention back at them from their own file is acted on where an outsider's reasoning is argued with. The skill gives no hint that the source you already have open is where to find it.
acceptance_criteria: Named as a technique in step 1, with the mechanism (conventions get stated once and not carried across) rather than just the instruction.
close_reason: Shipped for GH#7 as resolve_skill.py plus the step 1 rewrite; 8/8 behaviour cases pass including the reported 0.6.0-vs-0.10.0 scenario.

title: godot-game-ui: document the smoke-test harness shape and theme read-back (GH#5 item 4)
description: A test written as _init() + add_child() observes an empty Control (screens build in _ready), walks nothing, and reports ALL PASS. The working shape - _initialize(), root not get_root(), return false from _process for ~3 frames - is only discoverable by reading assets/smoke_test.gd. Also Label.get_theme_color_override() does not exist; the call that resolves an override is get_theme_color(&"font_color").
acceptance_criteria: Both UI SKILL.mds carry it; the vacuous-pass trap is named as a trap.
close_reason: Shipped for GH#5; verified by both smoke tests, juice_test, palette_lint on both kits, and a WCAG contrast probe across all six palettes.

title: godot-game-ui: scaffolder asserts 'nothing else hard-codes a colour' with nothing checking it (GH#5 item 2)
description: scaffold_ui.py:280 tells every user a property that was false in four files in 0.6.0. Same unchecked-assertion shape as the defect it describes. Pair it with palette_lint.py so the claim is one command away from being verified, in both scaffolders.
acceptance_criteria: Message points at the lint; both scaffolders match.
close_reason: Shipped for GH#5; verified by both smoke tests, juice_test, palette_lint on both kits, and a WCAG contrast probe across all six palettes.

title: kenney-asset-kit: SKILL.md 2D prose fixes (Vector/ as style reference, filtering caveat)
description: GH#6 items 2 and 3. (2) SKILL.md:188 describes Vector/ only as a resolution escape hatch; it is actually the style reference -- Kenney 2D packs are Flash exports, every path is fill=... stroke=none and the darker rim is a separate filled path underneath, not a stroke. A conforming new sprite can use an ordinary SVG stroke in the fill's darker shade and match. Say 'read it before drawing anything'. (3) SKILL.md:198 'Pixel-art packs need texture filtering set to nearest' has no counterexample -- vector packs (Tower Defense, Space Shooter) are anti-aliased and must stay on the default linear filter.
close_reason: kenney_probe2d.py shipped (probe + --check, stdlib PNG decode, segment-tolerance palette rule validated at tol=12 across 5 packs, 9 negative controls); SKILL.md 2D section rewritten with the Vector/ style reference, the linear-filter counterexample, and an 'Adding a sprite to a 2D pack' arm. CLAUDE.md, README, both manifests updated; version 0.10.0.

title: kenney-asset-kit: ship kenney_probe2d.py (probe + --check)
description: GH#6 item 1. The 2D half of kenney-asset-kit has no authoring or conformance arm: SKILL.md '## 5. Adding a model to a kit' is 3D-only and hands the gate to blender-mcp-modelling style_probe.py --check, which has no 2D equivalent. Ship scripts/kenney_probe2d.py, stdlib-only, mirroring kenney_probe.py: canvas size + uniformity, retina ratio, median/max opaque bbox, frequency-sorted palette, --json. Plus --check <candidate.png>: size, 2x retina counterpart, non-blank, centred, >=1px margin, every opaque colour on-palette. NON-OBVIOUS: 'on-palette' must mean 'within tolerance of the line SEGMENT between some pair of palette entries', not exact membership -- anti-aliased edges land between two flat fills and exact matching false-fails on Kenney's own sprites. Measured: worst legitimate blend 8.21, off-palette magenta control 188.50; tolerance 12 separates them.
close_reason: kenney_probe2d.py shipped (probe + --check, stdlib PNG decode, segment-tolerance palette rule validated at tol=12 across 5 packs, 9 negative controls); SKILL.md 2D section rewritten with the Vector/ style reference, the linear-filter counterexample, and an 'Adding a sprite to a 2D pack' arm. CLAUDE.md, README, both manifests updated; version 0.10.0.

title: godot-game-ui: palette is always the shipped amber; make the choice explicit per game vibe
description: The kit ships one warm amber PALETTE and nothing prompts a choice, so every scaffolded game comes out yellow. Add named palettes in references/palettes.md, a --palette flag on both scaffolders (parsing that file, mirroring the seed.py/axes.md convention), and SKILL.md guidance making the choice a required first step.
close_reason: Shipped in 0.8.0: six named palettes in references/palettes.md, --palette/--list-palettes on both scaffolders, SKILL.md guidance making the choice part of installing.

title: game-from-gibberish: seed.py mojibakes the em dash on Windows
description: GH#4. seed.py never pins sys.stdout encoding, so the em dash in the printed casting is written as cp1252 0x97 on a Windows console. Any UTF-8 consumer (pipe, redirect, subagent) sees a corrupted char, and SKILL.md step 3 says to copy that casting into SEED.md.
close_reason: Fixed in 8569118: pinned sys.stdout/stderr to UTF-8 with errors=replace. Verified 0x97 before, E2 80 94 after, casting content identical.

title: godot-game-ui: shell-screen button captions cannot be changed without forking the template
description: GH#3 defect 2. results_screen.gd, pause_menu.gd, title_screen.gd hardcode 'Play again'/'Main menu'/'Resume'/'Quit' etc. ResultsScreen already exports heading, so the title is configurable while the buttons are not. Export the captions with unchanged defaults.
close_reason: Fixed in 732054e: captions exported as again/menu/resume/restart/quit/play_label in both skills, defaults verbatim. Verified defaults + overrides in Godot 4.7.1.

title: godot-game-ui: backdrop colour is a literal in 4 templates, unreachable from the palette
description: GH#3 defect 1. results_screen.gd and title_screen.gd in both UI skills call UiTheme.backdrop(Color(0.06,0.05,0.07,1.0)) — an opaque near-copy of UiTheme.BACKDROP. Re-skinning the PALETTE block leaves the backdrop at the old colour, which is exactly what SKILL.md idea 1 forbids.
close_reason: Fixed in 2fc99b4: BACKDROP_OPAQUE, CHIP_INK, SLOT_EMPTY added to palette; 4 literal sites routed through them in both skills. Re-skin walk fails on all 4 pre-fix, passes post-fix; smoke+juice green.

title: release_check.py: assert the release metadata agrees with itself (log S-044)
description: Three releases this session, each bumping plugin.json and hand-editing README.md and CLAUDE.md. The descriptions in plugin.json and marketplace.json are documented as kept in sync by hand and nothing checks it.
acceptance_criteria: Asserts the two JSON descriptions match, the version parses and is bumped, and every skills/*/SKILL.md has name+description frontmatter.

title: Add a throwaway-Godot-project probe script (log S-038)
description: Verifying a .gd template change means: write project.godot, scaffold, --import, copy the test, --script, and read stderr rather than the exit code. CLAUDE.md documents the steps but there is no script, and --import (whose omission causes a parse-error cascade in files nobody touched) is the easiest to skip. Hand-rolled four times in the GH#5 session alone.
acceptance_criteria: One script that takes a skill name and prints the pass/fail lines for every test that kit ships, palette_lint included.

title: godot-game-ui: the kit has no text-contrast guarantee across palettes
description: Measured while fixing the clinical button bug. At full opacity, secondary-button ink sits below WCAG AA 4.5:1 in five of six palettes (amber 4.00, bloodmoon 3.85, candy 2.78, noir 3.69, verdant 3.58) and bloodmoon's primary is 2.65 - a saturated blood red takes neither black nor white ink well. Not a regression: amber was ~4.0 before this change too, and buttons are translucent over gameplay so raw bg_color overstates it. But nothing measures contrast at all, so a hand-written palette can ship unreadable. Options: a contrast arm on palette_lint (needs the compositing assumption pinned down), or tuning the palettes.
acceptance_criteria: Either a measured guarantee, or a documented statement that the kit does not make one and what to check by hand.

title: File [G-007] upstream: godot-selftest-harness lint --find-orphans is opt-in
description: log.md 2026-08-15 commit pass on plant-tower-defense, harness 0.19.0. Committing WIP that added Plant.set_selected() with no caller: plain lint and the 43-test suite both passed; --find-orphans caught it immediately (WARN: res://game/plant.gd: set_selected() has no reference outside its own file). Nothing prompts the flag and /verify does not pass it, so the default gate is green on a feature that cannot run. Proposed: run the orphan pass always, print a non-gating denominator line (Orphans: 0 of 24 script(s)) alongside Shaders:/UIDs:; or gate only on a public method new in the diff with no external reference. Distinct from SeveralHerr/godot-selftest-harness#7. File via skill-feedback-issue.
close_reason: Filed as SeveralHerr/godot-selftest-harness#11. Re-verified all three source claims against the installed 0.19.0 cache (84c7087) before filing; found two internal precedents in the repo's own docs that argue for the fix.
